correctness.rationale: Fold the circle by x=||t||. On [delta0,1/2] the induced distance map is bx-(b-1)/2 for odd b and b/2-bx for even b. In the odd case the allowed inverse branch fixes 1/2 and scales distances from it by 1/b. In the even case the two-step allowed folded interval is (delta,1/2-delta/b). The decreasing inverse y -> 1/2-y/b maps that interval into itself: its upper image endpoint is 1/2-delta/b and its lower one is delta0+delta/b^2 >= delta precisely up to the critical threshold. Thus every subsequent step scales length by 1/b; unfolding gives precisely two reflected intervals. The closed folded interval at equality collapses to the unique fixed distance b/[2(b+1)], attained by the stated two-cycle. In the odd case only 1/2 attains the maximal distance. Dividing nested Lebesgue probabilities gives the claimed conditional geometric tail, without independence. Separate exact breakpoint tests (python /workspace/independent_checks.py 1) passed 60 cases, including strict and non-strict critical boundaries, for five bases and horizons 2–4. The proof, not those tests, covers all bases and horizons.
